note: Asserted witnesses for the successor-declaration campaign. The CONTEXT file this campaign passes for `expect_from` is its own programs.json, so a witness can ask the chain which programs ran and compare that against the program map rather than against the binding that claims it.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.label | startswith("declare one release set")) | .error] | tostring
witnesses.provenance: Exactly one such transaction, and the chain reports no error on it. This is the only execution of `registry/lineage_v1::process` anywhere in this repository: the route has been dispatched in the deployed Registry since cohort-8 and until this campaign existed nothing recorded a single run of it, so a document with zero transactions -- which is what a preflight writes -- fails here rather than rendering as a witnessed route.

A cross-check between two files that do not read each other: every `Program <address> invoke [n]` line the chain wrote, at every depth, and the program map this campaign hands the census. The two subtracted addresses are Solana's own native program ids -- ComputeBudget, which the caller prepends a unit limit and price through, and the System program, which the Registry CPIs at depth two to allocate the 248-byte record. Everything else is first-party, and for this route there is exactly one of it. WRITTEN FIRST AND IT EARNED ITS KEEP ON THE FIRST RUN: the version of this witness that shipped in the first draft asked for the top-level invoke and asserted the route drove no CPI at all. The chain came back naming ComputeBudget, and the depth-two line naming System showed the second half was wrong too. The frame is two ComputeBudget instructions, one Registry instruction, and one System CPI beneath it -- which is what a route that CREATES an account looks like, and is now what this campaign claims.

`RELEASE_LINEAGE_BYTES_V1 = 248` in crates/dclutch-registry-contract, hex-encoded here, so 496 characters. This is not the code asserting its own constant: the caller read the account back off the chain after the send and refused to write this document unless the landed bytes were byte-equal to `projected_record` and its on-chain length equalled that constant. So the number checked here is the length of an account a validator wrote, arriving through a document that could not have been produced if the chain had disagreed.
